comment: kiln.ui.input's ownership rules (native/services/ui/input_own.h, 0.2.0-dev.31.13): the cases the native host test (tests/input_own_test.cpp) and the test kit's fake kiln.ui.input (managed/Kiln.TestKit/Fakes/UiInput, managed/tests/Kiln.TestKit.Tests/UiInputFakeTests.cs) both replay. Codes are KilnUiKey.vk in hex (2 the right button, 41 the A key, 20d a pad's B, 210 its left trigger, 100 a wheel notch); '@1' is controller 1. 'owners' subscribe in order; each takes the codes in 'take' ('*' = every press it is offered). Steps: down (a new press), repeat, up, focus (the window lost the focus), world (the client world changed), unsubscribe / disown (an owner went or gave up), leak (the game saw that press's down after all), mk (the MK_ bits hidden from the game must be this), pad (controller, the owned buttons' bits). Logs: 'game' what reaches the game, 'plain' what Kiln's other key and pointer subscribers and bindings get, and each owner's callbacks: press (offered, taken or not), repeat, release, end <why>.

cases.name: Blueprint owns a right-button gesture: press, held, release
a press the owner passes reaches the game and the others, its release too
an owned key's repeats and release go to the owner only
focus loss ends ownership: the owner hears it, a release that comes back later is the game's
a world change ends ownership; the release still reaches nobody (the game never saw the press)
unload (unsubscribe) mid-press: no callback, the release reaches nobody; the next press is everyone's
stuck-press guard: the game saw the down after all, so the release reaches it (the owner still hears it)
a new press without the release reaching Kiln ends the old claim as lost
the first owner to take a press owns it; a later owner never sees it
an owner only gets its own sources; the wheel is never ownable (a notch has no release)
a controller's buttons are owned per controller
an overlay that disowns its press as it closes: the release reaches nobody
the next press of an orphan (its world ended) is offered again
an owner that passes saw the press; the next owner takes it and keeps its release
